text: The common room smells of woodsmoke and spilled ale. By the fire, a sellsword is telling a story that gets less true with every cup.
It is a low, crooked place, kept by a man who counts every coin twice. Nobody here asks where your sword has been.
Rain drums on the shutters while a lone fiddler saws at a tune nobody asked for.
A faded notice by the door still offers a reward for a bandit who was hanged last spring. The keeper has never seen a reason to take it down.
The tavern has grown. A second hall now houses the sellswords, and word of the place travels with every caravan that stops here.
Every bench is taken tonight. Caravan drivers swap road news with mercenary captains over foaming tankards.
A travelling bard has the whole room stamping along to a song about a battle half of them claim to have fought in.
A second hearth roars at the far end of the hall, and the notice board is crowded with Guild seals now.
The tavern is known far and wide. Famous companies drink in its halls, and its cellars hold brews found nowhere else.
Banners of famous companies hang from the rafters, each one paid for in blood. Lords drink here under false names, and the keeper pretends not to know them.
The cellars run deeper than the foundations of some keeps. Tonight the keeper is pouring from a barrel older than the Empire.
Guild agents and foreign envoys share one long table with the costliest killers in the land. Somehow, nobody has drawn steel. Yet.
The room is in high spirits tonight: a hooded stranger in the corner has bought everyone a round, and nobody knows why.
It is a rowdy night. Out in the yard, two sellswords are wrestling, and half the room is shouting wagers at them.
The mood is sour tonight, and the keeper's is worst of all: someone has drunk the good barrel dry.
The room is buzzing tonight. A caravan has just come in off the road, and its drivers are full of news of armies on the move.
The tavern is full to bursting tonight: a wedding party has taken over the long table, and everyone is invited.
The room is on its best behaviour tonight. A Guild inspector sits by the door, scribbling in a little book and frowning at the prices.
The room has heard this one before. An old veteran is telling the tale of his greatest battle for the third time tonight, and it grows with every telling.
Water drips through the roof tonight, right over the best table, so the most dangerous man in the room is sitting in a puddle and daring anyone to laugh.
The keeper straightens up as we come in: "Back already, boss? Your usual seat is free."
The keeper nods to us as we come in: "Good to see you, boss. Business is steady."
The keeper pours a cup before we even reach the bar: "On the house, boss. Always."
The keeper leans over with a grin: "Drinks are paid for tonight, thanks to our friend in the corner. What else do you need?"
The keeper has to shout over the din: "Pay them no mind, it will be over soon enough. What do you need?"
The keeper glares past us at the empty barrel: "If you came for the good stuff, you are too late. What else?"
The keeper lowers his voice: "Plenty of talk of armies tonight. Yours, by the look of you?"
The keeper hands us a cup of the wedding wine: "On the bride's father, apparently. What do you need?"
The keeper speaks a little too politely: "Welcome, welcome. Everything here is in perfect order, as you can see."
The keeper rolls his eyes towards the old man: "Third time tonight. What do you need?"
The keeper keeps his face very straight: "Nobody laughs, nobody gets hurt. What do you need?"
The keeper turns to us as the story by the fire reaches its loudest part: "Don't believe a word of it. What do you need?"
The keeper finishes counting a stack of coins, then counts it again before looking up: "Well? What do you need?"
The keeper raises his voice over the fiddle: "Ignore him, he only knows the one tune. What do you need?"
The keeper follows our eyes to the old notice: "He's long gone, but it keeps the riff-raff honest. What do you need?"
The keeper waves us in: "Plenty of room since we built the second hall. What do you need?"
The keeper clears a corner of the bar for us: "Packed tonight, but there is always room for coin. What do you need?"
The keeper leans in so we can hear him over the singing: "He has been at it all night. What do you need?"
The keeper nods at the crowded board: "Guild work has never been better. What do you need?"
The keeper looks us over, as if weighing us against the famous companies in his halls: "Welcome. What do you need?"
The keeper does not ask our names: "Nobody here has one. What do you need?"
The keeper turns the tap of the ancient barrel with great care: "A cup of this costs more than a horse. What do you need?"
The keeper keeps one eye on the long table as he speaks: "Keep your hands where they can see them, and we will all get along. What do you need?"
